column4: S4.6: the original passes the address of a local (a stack slot) to a callee in two places: Voice_startPlayback (the `push ecx` slot given to Seq_listGetAt) and serviceChannelPlayback (`&b` given to DirectSoundDevice::duplicateBuffer / freeBufferById), and Voice::update keeps three more (the node out slot, the [esp+0x14] slot given to helper 0x139d / playEvent, the [esp+0x20] slot of its second walk). The port context has no stack, and the emulator's own stack is not mapped into it (U-1413). frame_cell() uses 16-byte cells in the padding after sound.dll's last section (image offset SizeOfImage - 0x100, never read or written by the module: the last section .reloc ends at rva 0xbdd12), which is mapped in both the port and the emulator. The cells hold the same values the stack slots held, so the results equal the original's; the cells are not part of any compared region.

column4: S4.6: Unicorn's x87 keeps a signaling NaN signaling through fld / fst (qword and dword), the CPU sets the quiet bit (Intel SDM, FLD: the masked invalid-operation response converts an SNaN source to a QNaN) and so did the live C3 A/B (log/c3/c3fe_notes.txt: Channel_startVoice with the +0x1388 double copied as raw bits, no quieting, read RED). The port quiets (quiet64 / quiet32 where the original loads through the x87). For the keys of updateVoiceRate, Channel_startVoice, serviceChannelPlayback and Channel_allocAndInitVoice the oracle forgives a difference that is exactly the quiet bit of a NaN pattern (port set, emulator clear) and the golden digest of such a vector pins the port's regions; any other difference still fails. Counts: golden quirk field per key (port/test/golden_audio_chan.json). Not forgiven: a port that quiets where the original moves raw bits (the golden would then hold the quieted bytes: the control is the live c3fe one, not this file).

column4: S4.6: the c3fh caller-word keys (Channel_setRate, Channel_recomputeVoiceGains, Channel_setReverseRate, Channel_stepVolumeFade, Voice_resetDefaults at x87 control word 0x0f7f) cannot run in the x64 library (SG_E_UNSUPPORTED for any word but the 0x027f equivalents) and the live oracle's host callback does not cross the Win32 runner's pipe (U-1412 area). The oracle records their bundle and golden digests from the emulated original at the word the emulator held (read from Unicorn's FPCW per vector), the x64 replay skips those vectors, and the Win32 replay (bundles + script host) applies the word with sg_set_fpcw and must equal the golden. A vector the word changes reads RED on x64 by design (counted in the oracle log as X87_WIN32).
